title: Universal quantum processors in spin systems via robust local pulse sequences
authors: Matteo Votto; Johannes Zeiher; Benoît Vermersch
abstract: We propose a protocol to realize quantum simulation and computation in spin systems with long-range interactions. Our approach relies on the local addressing of single spins with external fields parametrized by Walsh functions. This enables a mapping from a class of target Hamiltonians, defined by the graph structure of their interactions, to pulse sequences. We then obtain a recipe to implement arbitrary two-body Hamiltonians and universal quantum circuits. Performance guarantees are provided in terms of bounds on Trotter errors and total number of pulses. Additionally, Walsh pulse sequences are shown to be robust against various types of pulse errors, in contrast to previous hybrid digital-analog schemes of quantum computation. We demonstrate and numerically benchmark our protocol with examples from the dynamics of spin models, quantum error correction and quantum optimization algorithms.

D Approximation scheme for shorter Walsh sequences
In this section we investigate the unitary error due to imposing a cut-off Λw to the Walsh indices.
We will focus on one-dimensional systems, even though we believe this approach can be extended to
higher dimensional systems. We consider the case in which the target Hamiltonian H̃ has finite range
interactions, i.e. there exists a distance r = O(1) such that J˜ij = 0 if |i − j| > r. In general, the Walsh
sequence realizing the dynamics of H̃ in AHT will have a length n = O(N ). However, the length can
be reduced by assuming that interactions in the resource Hamiltonian HR are negligible after a certain
distance Λr ≥ r (for resource Hamiltonians with couplings Eq. (6) it is the case if α is large). In this
case, we do not require using different Walsh indices to decouple two qubits that are separated by
distance larger than Λr . Formally, this means that Eq. (11) becomes

     E(G1X ) = {(i, j) | xi = xj and |i − j| < Λr }, E(G1Y ) = {(i, j) | yi = yj and |i − j| < Λr } .              (87)

Fixing the distance cut-off Λr provides us with a strategy to reduce the pulse sequence length (see
Fig. 7):

 1. order the values of Walsh indices xi ;

 2. divide the N qubits in the subregions Al , such that [lΛr + 1, (l + 1)Λr ] ∈ Al , in such a way that
    links can only be present between Al and Al+1 ;

 3. assign sequentially (the first xi to the 1st qubit) the Walsh indices to A1 and A2 ;

 4. assign sequentially the Walsh indices to A3 starting from the beginning (i.e. from those in A1 ),
    but excluding those already assigned in A2

 5. repeat, where in any Al are excluded the Walsh indices in Al−1 .
